title: fix(metadata-admin): the page-block and hook condition editors lint in the scope their runtime binds (objectui#8167)
body:
Part of #8167

⚠️ **Deliberately `Part of`, not `Fixes`.** Only ONE of the ruling's three arms ships here. A closing keyword would shut the card over the two that do not.

> **Revised after contract review — `5706686234` returned VERDICT: FAIL on the page-block arm, and it was right.** That arm has been withdrawn; the body below describes what the branch now contains. The history of the reversal is in the commits, not hidden by this edit.

---

## What ships: the hook arm

`@objectstack/objectql`'s `wrapDeclarativeHook` compiles a hook `condition` once and evaluates it as

```ts
const r = ExpressionEngine.evaluate<boolean>(expr, { record: record ?? {}, previous });
```

`record` and `previous`, and nothing else; the next lines throw `HookConditionError` rather than resolving false (*"Fail LOUD. Not `false`"*, objectstack#4775). The editor linted `flattened`, so a bare `status == 'done'` came back clean — and on this surface the consequence is worse than a dead gate: **the author's write pays for the editor's success receipt.** The mount now passes `scope="record"`.

**`previous` needed no work, and that is a measurement.** The ruling wrote 「`previous` added to the lint scope's known roots」 as though it were a line of work. It is already there:

```
scope 'record' · "previous.status != record.status"  ->  errors: [], warnings: []
introspectScope('predicate', { scope: 'record' }).roots
  -> ["record","previous","input","os","current_user","user","vars"]
```

A new case pins the transition idiom so a later narrowing cannot take it away in silence.

## ⛔ What was withdrawn: the page-block arm, and why it cannot be fixed at the mount

The renderer reading was correct as far as it went — `SchemaRenderer` binds the row as the `record` root, so a bare `status == 'done'` never matches on a page block. **What it missed is in the very expression it quoted**: the same evaluator construction also binds `page: pageVariables`.

At `scope: 'record'` the validator runs a strict environment declaring exactly the engine's `SCOPE_ROOTS`, and `page` is not in it. Measured on the installed `@objectstack/formula`, all four corners:

| scope | source | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `flattened` | `status == 'done'` | clean — **the defect the card is about** |
| `flattened` | `page.selectedProjectId != ''` | clean |
| `record` | `status == 'done'` | error naming `record.status` — right |
| `record` | `page.selectedProjectId != ''` | **error: "bare reference `page` … Write `record.page`."** |

That last row is `@objectstack/spec`'s **own worked example**: `page.zod.ts` describes `visibleWhen` as *"Contract-bound roots: `record`, `current_user` … and page state as `page.<var>`"* and ends with `e.g. "page.selectedProjectId != ''"`. And because this inspector reports blocking CEL issues upward, where the host counts them, that error **disables Save and auto-save while the block is selected**.

⇒ neither lint scope fits this mount. `flattened` accepts the bare-field defect; `record` refuses a contract-bound root with a nonsense remedy. This is the **objectui#8155 shape** (`app` refused although bound). The mount goes back to passing nothing — `flattened` being the less-wrong of two wrong answers, an editor that over-accepts rather than one that refuses what the spec documents.

**The reading is kept, corrected.** The comment at the mount now names all three bound roots and says in as many words that neither scope expresses that set, so the next reader does not re-derive the measurement and reach the same wrong conclusion.

**Blocked on the engine, not on this PR.** Making that mount lintable needs either `page` among `@objectstack/formula`'s scope roots — its own docblock says the list errs toward declaring more, and that a missing root is a false positive — or a per-surface root allowlist on `validateExpression`. That is an **objectstack spec-seat** change carrying its own clause-② review. ⛔ Not opened from here; carried back to the card for the seat.

## ⛔ Still not shipped: the `ConditionWidget` arm

Unchanged from the first round and upheld by the review. `ConditionWidget` has **zero** mount sites — it is resolved from a registry by field-name convention behind `WidgetRenderer = (props: WidgetProps) => React.ReactElement`, so `satisfies Record<string, WidgetRenderer>` makes a widget-specific required prop a compile error at the registry. `FormFieldSpec.scope` would be born declared-and-unenforced (zero in-tree form specs declare a condition field); `WidgetContext.conditionScope` hard-codes one scope inside the generic `ResourceEditPage` unless derived per metadata type; a required prop on the **published** `SchemaForm` is a break across ~70 call sites. The choice is the director's — costed in the report on the card. `widgets.tsx` is **untouched**.

## The fence, verified

| mount | scope | status |
|:--|:--|:--|
| hook `condition` | `record` | **changed here** |
| page block `visibleWhen` | flattened | unchanged — withdrawn, blocked on the engine |
| `widgets.tsx` (`ConditionWidget`) | flattened | unchanged — arm open |
| `PermissionAdvancedFacets` (RLS) | flattened | unchanged — CORRECT (#5738 stand-down 3) |
| `FlowNodeConfigField` (flow node) | flattened | unchanged — flow tier is not a row surface |
| `ConditionBuilder`'s own default | `undefined` → `hint.scope ?? 'flattened'` | identical; the prop stays **optional** |

No component API changes. Production wiring in this branch is exactly **one line**.

## Verification — re-run on `d519436`

Every heavy run through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=objectui-8167-dev`); verdicts read from the lock's own `VERDICT command-exit` line, exit codes redirected to a file and read back, never through a pipe.

**Pins** — `ConditionBuilder.mountScope.test.tsx`, real `@objectstack/formula`, no stub: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 11 passed (11)`, exit 0.

**Ablation, two legs, both directions predicted before running.** `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with `REPO_ROOT`-absolute restore; HEAD blob hashes resolved non-empty first (`2b4b1183…`, `7c26cca5…`).

```
LEG A — remove the HOOK wiring (predict RED, 1 case)
  on-disk proof: scope="record" HK 1 -> 0 · git diff --stat: 1 file changed, 1 deletion
  Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
  × rejects the bare shorthand in a hook condition and names the record.FIELD fix
  failure mode is the DEFECT: AssertionError: expected null to be 'true' (aria-invalid null)
  restore: git diff HEAD EMPTY · count back to 1

LEG B — ADD scope="record" to the PAGE BLOCK (predict RED, the page.VAR pin)
  on-disk proof: scope="record" PB 0 -> 1 · git diff --stat: 1 file changed, 1 insertion
  Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
  × accepts the spec's own `page.VAR` example — which the `record` scope would refuse
  failure message is the review's refusal, rendered in the designer:
    "bare reference `page` … Write `record.page`."
  restore: git diff HEAD EMPTY · count back to 0
```

Leg B is the point of the replacement pin: the withdrawal is now **falsifiable**, not asserted. Anyone who "settles" that mount with `'record'` gets a red test carrying the nonsense remedy, instead of a designer with a disabled Save button.

**Affected tests** — the 32 files naming `PageBlockInspector`, `HookDefaultInspector` or `ConditionBuilder` (`git grep -lw`): `Test Files 32 passed (32)` / `Tests 347 passed (347)`, exit 0.

**Type-check** — `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, exit 0, zero `error TS` lines; the script echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. Prerequisite built first: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` → `28 successful, 28 total`.

**Lint — NARROWING DECLARED, three pieces of evidence:** ① `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint` across every package; what ran is app-shell's own complete CI unit, the only package this diff touches. ② **1168** files, **0 errors**, 3026 warnings — counts read from `--format json`. ③ Invariance: `eslint.config.js` configures no `projectService` and no `project:`, so no type-aware linting exists and a change inside app-shell cannot move another package's verdict.

**Derived gates** (hand-derived from `package.json` + `.github/workflows/`; objectui has no `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`) — all exit 0: `check:control-bytes` (*scanned 7762 tracked text file(s)*), `check:new-line-citations` (*0 new citation(s)*), `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:governed-queue-guard`, `changeset:check`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` (*3 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)*), `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all four paths → **NOT GOVERNED**. Out-of-band control-byte scan of the diff → no hits.

**Changeset re-scoped** to the hook arm. The withdrawn sentence the review flagged (*"Nothing already saved changes meaning"*) is gone as a blanket claim; the text now describes one mount, and states that the page-block mount is unchanged and why.

**NOT MEASURED:** remote CI on this head — reported at local-verification close; no waiting, no polling.

**Carriers:** both were stripped by the seat after the FAIL. ⛔ Not re-hung from here — a fresh clause-② review is the seat's to commission on this head.
